reading.body:
Riley Ohlson is named on 7 AI lobbying filings, all filed through one firm, all for a single client, the AFL-CIO.

The record is narrow and consistent. Seven filings, one firm, one client, and 19 distinct bills named across them. Every bill entry carries the same qualifier: named in an AI filing listing this lobbyist, for 2025 or later. That means the AI subject matter is what ties these bills together here, not any claim that each bill is itself an AI bill.

For AI specifically, this is one labor union's disclosed federal lobbying footprint on AI-related legislation, routed through one firm and one registered lobbyist. It shows the AFL-CIO is engaging the AI bill space directly rather than only through trade associations or coalitions. It says nothing about what the filings advocate, whether the positions succeeded, or how much was spent.

What the data does not cover matters as much as what it does. There is no spend figure, no filing date, no bill title, and no text of any filing. The count of 7 filings and the count of 19 bills are different measures and should not be conflated. A separate lobbyist shares the name, so this record should not be merged with that one.
